body.p: For styling beyond what themes provide, the custom CSSepub.custom.css parameter lets you append your own stylesheet. It is loaded last in the cascade, so it overrides all other styles:

section.title: CSS Custom Properties
section.p: All themes define their visual characteristics through CSS variablesCSS custom properties on the :root selector. This means you can change colors, fonts, and spacing by overriding just the variables you care about, without rewriting entire rule sets.
For example, to change the accent color and body font across the entire EPUB:
section.note: See Appendix C: CSS Variables Reference for a complete list of all available variables and their default values.

section.title: Sidebars and Pull Quotes
section.p: sidebaroutputclassSections with outputclass="sidebar" are transformed into styled <aside> elements with a distinct background. This is useful for supplementary content, pull quotes, and "Did You Know?" boxes:
section.codeblock:
Did You Know?

EPUB 3.3 became a W3C Recommendation in May 2023.
section.p: The sidebar background color is controlled by the --color-background-sidebar CSS variable (default: #f5f5f5).

section.title: Platform-Specific Considerations
section.p: Different reading systems have varying levels of CSS support. The epub-platform-{name}.css stylesheets address known rendering quirks:

ul.li: KDP (Kindle) — Adjusts image maximum widths, reduces margins for smaller Kindle screens, and works around Kindle's limited CSS variable support
Apple Books — Enables -webkit prefixed properties for optimal rendering on iOS and macOS
Generic — No platform-specific overrides; uses only standard EPUB 3.3 CSS
